subject: Action required: verify your DocuSign account
top_finding: A link points at a lookalike domain

message.subject: Action required: verify your DocuSign account
message.excerpt: Dear customer, we noticed unusual activity on case 728065. Verify your account today: https://docusign-alert.example/alert/728065

findings.title: A link points at a lookalike domain
evidence: Link to docusign-alert[.]example wraps the name from docusign[.]com in extra words (imitating DocuSign)
findings.lesson: Hover before you click. The link's domain, not its text, tells you where you'll land.

findings.title: Sender domain imitates a known domain
evidence: Sender domain docusign-alert[.]example wraps the name from docusign[.]com in extra words (imitating DocuSign)
findings.lesson: Read the domain letter by letter. Attackers register names that look right at a glance.

findings.title: Link text shows one site, link goes to another
evidence: Link reads "Sign in to docusign[.]com" but goes to docusign-alert[.]example
findings.lesson: What a link says and where it goes can differ. Hover to see the real destination before clicking.

findings.title: Sender failed DMARC
evidence: DMARC failed for docusign-alert[.]example (domain policy: reject)
findings.lesson: A failed sender check means the message may be forged. If it claims to be from someone you know, confirm with them another way.

findings.title: Display name poses as a brand
evidence: Display name "DocuSign Support" claims DocuSign, sent from docusign-alert[.]example
findings.lesson: The name on a message is free text. Check the address, not just who it says it is.

findings.title: Talks as a brand, links nowhere near it
evidence: Opens as DocuSign but neither the sender nor any link uses a domain that belongs to it
findings.lesson: When a message says it's from a well-known company, go to that company's site yourself instead of using the link.

findings.title: SPF or DKIM check failed
evidence: SPF did not pass for docusign-alert[.]example
findings.lesson: Real mail from a company is signed. Failed signatures are one more reason to slow down.

findings.title: Generic greeting on an account message
evidence: Greets a 'valued customer/user' while asking about account access
findings.lesson: Messages from a service you use usually know your name. 'Dear customer' is a tell.
